story.title: Story 1: Thread, Actor, Message, And Part Store

result.reviewScopeSummary: Reviewed Story 1’s thread/actor/message/part store foundation and the bundled Chunk 1 generated-session metadata surfaces: story/spec docs, the shared domain helpers, `ThreadStore`/`FileThreadStore`, `thread-service`, test fixtures/temp-store helpers, and the `foundation` plus `thread-store` test suites. Ran the configured story gate and epic gate sequentially after code review.

newFindings.title: Concurrent appends can invert canonical source order under load
newFindings.evidence: `appendSourceMessage` performs async actor declaration before handing work to the store (`src/context-steward/services/thread-service.ts:129-140`), while the only serialization point is `FileThreadStore.withThreadMutation` inside `appendMessage` (`src/context-steward/store/file-thread-store.ts:292-342`, `src/context-steward/store/file-thread-store.ts:595-618`). That means overlapping callers can enter the per-thread queue in a different order than invocation order and receive swapped `sourceOrder` values. The shipped concurrency test covers this contract (`tests/context-steward/thread-store.test.ts:440-489`); it failed once during verification stress with `message-concurrent-002` stored before `message-concurrent-001`. A focused 100-run real-store reproduction against the same code path reported `{"runs":100,"mismatches":16}` for the first caller not receiving `sourceOrder = 1`. This breaks the story’s canonical ordering guarantee for source messages.

productionPathFindings: SV-01: the real file-backed append path can assign canonical `sourceOrder` in the wrong order when overlapping callers race before queue acquisition.
additionalObservations: Sequential `npm run verify` and `npm run verify-all` both passed; the blocking issue came from direct stress of the real concurrent append path rather than a deterministic gate failure.
`npm run verify-all` currently passes with `No integration tests found.`, so the planned `file-thread-store.integration.test.ts` smoke coverage is still absent from the repo.
No fake adapters, shim branches, or placeholder runtime paths were identified in the reviewed production code.
